source.title: Concept Component Analysis: A Principled Approach for Concept Extraction in LLMs
source.authors: Yu-Hang Liu; Er-Dun Gao; Dong Gong; Anton van den Hengel; J. Shi

record.tranche_reason: The study tests the functional consequences of replacing model activations with SAE reconstructions using activation-patching metrics, but does not analyze SAE residual structure using the original claim’s measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports SAE reconstruction MSE and comparisons with ConCA, but those results do not test linear predictability, error scaling across SAE sizes, or the composition of dark matter. Activation-patching results bear on functional consequences of omitting the SAE reconstruction error. No loss-versus-random-error comparison is reported.
record.test_reason: A ConCA method paper using SAEs only as baselines. It never analyses the SAE error vector: no linear prediction of the error, no scaling across SAE sizes, no random-error control, no linear/nonlinear split, no restoring of the error term. The patching results (Appendix O) compare its own method with SAE baselines on final-layer output fidelity. They are figure-only and do not measure any version's effect. It does not cite the original.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but narrow. Overall, the authors conclude that LLM representations approximate linear mixtures of concept log-posteriors. They conclude that ConCA beats SAE variants in faithfulness (concept correlation, patching) and utility (few-shot and OOD probing). In patching, ConCA-BatchNorm is best and top-k and batch-top-k SAEs diverge most.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares SAE and ConCA reconstructions using activation patching, rather than measuring dark-matter error predictability or comparing reconstruction harm with random errors of matched size.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported functional comparison is on Pythia-70m; the authors state ConCA-BatchNorm performs best overall, while SAE-top-k and SAE-batch-top-k show the largest divergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching SAE reconstructions into Pythia-70m's final hidden layer changes output predictions. Top-k and batch-top-k SAEs show the largest divergence; ConCA variants show less. Figure only, no random-error control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final-layer SAE reconstructions distort next-token predictions more than ConCA reconstructions, with the size of the distortion depending on the SAE variant.

fits_no_version.finding: Reconstruction MSE varies about threefold across SAE training schemes at equal width. On Pythia-70m: TopK ≈22.9, Batch-TopK ≈24.6, Panneal ≈7.7 (Table 5). This is total error, not decomposed dark matter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction error magnitude depends strongly on the sparsity mechanism or training scheme.

record.problems: The relevant activation-patching results are presented in a figure without numerical values in the text. The comparison uses no random-error control and does not directly test whether restoring the SAE error term recovers behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant results left out. SAE reconstruction MSE and feature-alignment results are not rows for the tested version because they do not measure functional effects of omitted SAE error.

untested.parts: All: no regression of SAE error on input activations.
All: one SAE size (2^15), no per-token error-norm analysis.
All: no comparison with random errors of matched norm.
All: no decomposition of the error.
All: no circuit or steering analysis and no error-term restoration.
All: no dark-matter measurement across architectures or training objectives.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked V5 tested with a supports label. That is unwarranted: the patching measures overall reconstruction fidelity against a competitor method, not whether SAE-based analyses lose behaviour without the error term. Values are figure-only. Only the last layer of Pythia-70m is used.

versions.untested_parts: Linear predictability of SAE error from input activations.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, overlap of failing contexts, and persistence of error with scale.
The study reports output-logit distortion, not model loss compared with random errors of the same size.
No division of SAE error into linear and nonlinear components or tests of their learnability.

Tests output changes from replacing activations with reconstructions, but does not test circuits or steering, restore the error term as an intervention, or quantify the share of behavior carried by that term.
No direct test of whether dark matter is caused by SAE training choices or shrinks with improved SAE architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: Pythia-70m
rows.operation_detail: Replace sampled hidden activations with SAE-top-k reconstructions, then compare output logits with those from the original activations.
rows.measure: Argmax Match: whether the top predicted token stays the same
rows.note: The text says SAE-top-k is among the methods with the largest divergence; no numerical match rate is stated.
rows.check: Method-vs-baseline comparison (ConCA vs SAE), figure only. No random-error control, so not V3. No circuit/steering analysis or error restoration, so not V5.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Pythia-70m, SAE-top-k and SAE-batch-top-k reconstructions on the sampled activations
reader_labels.reason: The authors report these SAE variants show the largest output divergence, indicating functional mismatch after reconstruction (r1–r6). The reported measures do not quantify the share of behavior lost or test restoring the error term.
